result: Global Malat1 knockout mice (Malat1-/-) exhibit significantly reduced trabecular bone mass with decreased osteoblast-mediated bone formation and increased osteoclast-mediated bone resorption, while cortical bone remains normal. This uncoupling of bone remodeling establishes Malat1 as a novel regulator of bone homeostasis.
evaluation: All reviewers accepted these findings without challenge. Reviewer 1 stated the authors 'carefully analyzed the role of Malat1 with both in vivo and in vitro system' and that 'the conclusion of this paper is mostly well supported by data.' Reviewer 2 noted 'the bone phenotype of osteoblast-specific Malat1 knockout mice is of high interest,' implicitly accepting the global knockout phenotype as well. The editor described this as 'an important and convincing dataset.'

result: Osteoblast-specific conditional knockout of Malat1 (Malat1 cKOOcn) recapitulates the osteoporotic phenotype of global knockout mice with reduced trabecular bone formation, demonstrating that Malat1 is a cell-intrinsic osteogenic regulator in osteoblasts.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly praised this finding. Reviewer 2 stated 'the bone phenotype of osteoblast-specific Malat1 knockout mice is of high interest' and noted the manuscript is 'well-written and data are presented in a clear and easily understandable manner.' Reviewer 1 noted the authors 'generated global and conditional KO mice in osteoblast and osteoclast lineage cells' and found the conclusions 'mostly well supported by data.'

result: Malat1 binds to β-catenin in osteoblasts and enhances β-catenin transcriptional activity without affecting its nuclear translocation. Malat1 deficiency reduces expression of β-catenin target genes, indicating Malat1 acts as a scaffold to tether β-catenin in nuclei and positively regulate Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
evaluation: Reviewers strongly endorsed this mechanistic finding. Reviewer 2 stated 'the role of Malat1 in controlling beta-catenin activity and OPG expression is interesting and novel.' The editor emphasized this work 'supports a role and mechanism for beta-catenin that is novel and unusual' and is 'of value to areas other than the bone field.' No concerns were raised about the ChIRP, RIP, or luciferase assay data.

result: Malat1 deletion in osteoclast lineage cells (Malat1 cKOLyz2) does not affect osteoclast differentiation, function, or bone mass in vitro or in vivo, demonstrating that Malat1 does not directly regulate osteoclastogenesis but inhibits it through non-autonomous mechanisms.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this finding despite initial questions. Reviewer 2 initially noted 'the lack of a bone phenotype when Malat1 is deleted with LysM-Cre is of interest given the previous report suggesting a role for this lncRNA in osteoclasts' but stated in the revised version that 'all previous comments have been addressed in a satisfactory manner.' Reviewer 1 found it 'more interesting' that Malat1 deletion in osteoclast lineage cells 'does not affect osteoclast differentiation and function.'

result: Malat1 regulates osteoclastogenesis through osteoblast-osteoclast crosstalk by controlling OPG expression in osteoblasts. Malat1-deficient osteoblasts show decreased OPG but not RANKL expression, leading to increased RANKL/OPG ratio and enhanced osteoclast formation. Local bone marrow OPG levels are decreased while serum OPG remains normal, and exogenous OPG rescues the excessive osteoclastogenesis.
evaluation: Reviewers endorsed this mechanism. Reviewer 2 stated 'the role of Malat1 in controlling beta-catenin activity and OPG expression is interesting and novel.' Reviewer 1 noted the authors 'found that Malat1 acts as an co-activator of b-Catenin directly regulating osteoblast activity and indirectly regulating osteoclast activity via mediating OPG.' The rescue experiments with exogenous OPG were not challenged.

result: Chondrocytes are an important cellular source of OPG in bone. Malat1 regulates OPG and Jagged1 expression in chondrocytes through β-catenin signaling, with Malat1-/- chondrocytes showing ~50% reduction in OPG and other β-catenin target genes. This chondrocyte-osteoclast crosstalk contributes to enhanced osteoclast formation in Malat1-/- mice.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this novel finding after initial concerns were addressed. Reviewer 2 initially questioned 'the role of Malat1 and OPG in chondrocytes is unclear since the osteocalcin-Cre mice (which should retain normal Malat1 levels in chondrocytes) have similar bone loss as the global mutants,' but stated in the revised version that 'all previous comments have been addressed in a satisfactory manner.' The scRNAseq analysis identifying chondrocytes as OPG-expressing cells was not challenged.

result: Malat1 deficiency in both global knockout and osteoblast-specific conditional knockout mice significantly impairs bone regeneration in a femoral fracture model at 21 days post-fracture, demonstrating that Malat1 in osteoblasts plays an important role in fracture healing.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this finding after revisions. Reviewer 2 initially noted 'the data in the fracture model in Figure 8 is enhanced with quantitative data' but stated in the revised version that 'all previous comments have been addressed in a satisfactory manner.' The editor noted 'revisions further improved the paper and addressed the reviewers' concerns.'

result: Malat1-/- mice show no growth retardation, macroscopic differences, or cortical bone abnormalities, with cortical bone parameters remaining normal in both global and conditional knockout models.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge these observations. The lack of cortical bone phenotype was presented as supporting data distinguishing trabecular from cortical bone effects, and no reviewer questioned these findings. This is consistent with the reviewers' overall acceptance of the careful phenotypic characterization.
